shortDescription: Thailand's central bank chief said on Thursday there is no rush to raise interest rates and monetary policy could not address structural issues constraining economic growth.

children: Thailand's central bank chief said on Thursday there is no rush to raise interest rates and monetary policy could not address structural issues constraining economic growth.
The central bank left its key interest rate unchanged at 1.00% in August and its next monetary policy review is on October 28
Addressing a business forum on Thursday, Bank of Thailand Governor Vitai Ratanakorn said the economy was seen growing about 2.3% this year
Exports were expected to grow 17% to 18% this year, up from the 14% expansion seen earlier, he added
Inflation would likely slow to around 2% in 2026, from June's forecast of 2.8%, Vitai said
